summary: JSON Stream Parser: turns stream fragments into JSON values as NDJSON, concatenated values, or one whole document.
description: Each `parse` appends the current `chunk` to a buffer and extracts whatever is now complete. 'NDJSON' takes one value per line and reports a line that does not parse rather than skipping it silently. 'Stream' accepts any concatenation of complete top-level values — whitespace-separated objects, or a JSON array whose elements are emitted as they close — and is safe at every chunk boundary, including one that falls inside a string. 'Single document' holds everything back until the whole buffer is one complete value, then emits it. Text that is not yet a complete value stays in the buffer and shows on `pendingCharacters`; `maxLength` stops a malformed stream from growing without bound by clearing the buffer and reporting it. `values` carries everything the last parse completed, `parsed` the last of them.
whenToUse: A stream whose payloads are JSON but do not arrive one-per-event: NDJSON logs, a chunked HTTP body, an array streamed element by element. Not needed for Server-Sent Events with one JSON object per event — that node already parses each payload onto its Data output.

ports.chunk: The fragment to append. Empty chunks are ignored, so a Parse with nothing new re-tries the existing buffer.
ports.format: 'NDJSON' for line-delimited, 'Stream' for concatenated values and streamed arrays, 'Single document' to wait for one whole value.
ports.maxLength: Cap on unparsed text. Exceeding it clears the buffer and reports an error, which almost always means the wrong Format.
ports.parsed: The last value completed by the most recent Parse.
ports.values: Every value completed by the most recent Parse, in order. Wire this to For Each when a chunk can complete several.
ports.valueCount: Running total across all parses, not the size of the last batch.
ports.pendingCharacters: Text held back because a value is incomplete. Persistently non-zero means the Format does not match the stream.
ports.isComplete: True when the last Parse left nothing buffered.
ports.success: Fires only when the Parse produced at least one value, so an advancing-but-incomplete chunk stays quiet.
ports.failure: Fires per malformed value; the stream keeps going rather than stalling on one bad record.

patterns: Server-Sent Events `data` → `chunk`, `onMessage` → `parse`, format NDJSON: a log stream that arrives several lines per event.
`values` → For Each `items` renders everything a chunk completed, instead of only the last value.
`pendingCharacters` on a debug Text output makes a format mismatch obvious instead of looking like a dead stream.
antiPatterns: Using 'Single document' on a never-ending stream — the buffer grows until Max Pending trips.
Reading only `parsed` when a chunk can complete several values; the earlier ones are then silently ignored.
Adding this after Server-Sent Events when each event is already one JSON object — the SSE node's Data output has parsed it.
